description:
Could You Live at the Moon's South Pole?

Episode 79 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌑
The Moon's south pole: craters in permanent shadow, colder than minus 200 degrees Celsius, hide water ice. India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the south pole in 2023, and NASA plans to land astronauts there on Artemis IV, targeted for 2028.

➡️ Next stop: Ceres
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #moonsouthpole #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Could you live on the Moon? Everyone wants to go to one spot. Here's why.
Every human who walked on the Moon landed near its equator. But everyone wants to go to its south pole now. Why?
segments.headline: Why the south pole?

segments.text: At the poles, the Sun always skims the horizon. The bottoms of some deep craters haven't seen sunlight in billions of years.
segments.headline: Never seen sunlight

segments.text: They're among the coldest places in the solar system, colder than minus two hundred degrees Celsius.
And in that cold, there's ice. Water, frozen in the dark.
segments.headline: Water ice

segments.text: Water means drinking water for astronauts, and it can be split into oxygen to breathe, and fuel for rockets.
segments.headline: Water = air and fuel

segments.text: In August twenty twenty-three, India's Chandrayaan three became the first mission to land near the south pole.
segments.headline: Chandrayaan-3, 2023

segments.text: NASA plans to land astronauts there on Artemis four, targeted for twenty twenty-eight. Artemis three will first test the landers in Earth orbit.
segments.headline: Artemis: humans next

segments.text: China is also planning crewed landings and a research base near the south pole.
segments.headline: A new race

segments.text: Next stop: Ceres. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
